- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.68) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days); apply dampening factor to subsequent forecasts.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3-5 consecutive forecasts are above 70, reduce by 1-2% per day; if below 65, increase by 1-2% per day.
- Forecast horizon 30d: model tends to be too optimistic in early days (1-5), then too pessimistic in late days (25-30); apply asymmetric correction: +0.5% for early, -0.5% for late.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., +0.68, -0.33, +0.68), model often misreads momentum; align forecast with sentiment cycle direction.
